notes.title: Big Huge Update - ROGUELITE
notes.notes:
[h2]I've been working on this update for a few months, stoked to finally release the baby-form of what this game will become.[/h2]

[h2]After some trial and error I've landed on a procedural level-generator that I'm very happy with. You can [url=https://youtu.be/LcPtE-_QfUo]see the previous and current versions here[/url][/h2]


This new grid-based random-room system is going to allow for a crazy amount of unique levels, while still having handcrafted rooms, traps and challenges. The first version of these levels is the Lab setting, but I've got plenty more on the way (including a Missing No. version, which will smash all the different settings together into a weirdo franken-level).

Some gameplay of the new level system in action:

[previewyoutube=Sj0t3kYM7R0;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]












In addition to the level change-up, I've added some more upgrades and mechanics. 

[h2]First up we have the flammability[/h2]

Every monster and every object now has a flammability rating (as well as a "wet" rating, but let's stay on topic). This makes them less or more likely to catch fire naturally from environmental fire sources. The most obvious result: Set fire to some boxes, and watch enemies catch fire. Fun!
[i]The wet / flammable system is going to be developed further in the background with things like Water Bombs, Electricity Effects, etc etc etc[/i]

But this is also going to play into the rare-enemy mutations- some will be impervious to getting lit. Some will PREFER to be on fire and suffer no damage. 

There's also a new Passive upgrade which turns any weapon you have equipped into a fire-variant. First level yields a 50% chance to ignite. Second level = Fire All the Time.

This combos in some interesting ways, especially with the Wifflebat, which has no real damage, but high knockback. It's designed to be used with all the projectiles in the environment, and if it has the fire-upgrade, these turn into flaming projectiles. Pretty fun!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/7d2bd017ef3fed31b77b4554919b69272ee962ab.gif[/img]


[h2]New Passives[/h2]
Plenty more on the way, but here are a few new ones

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/1cb0982ff2b21d1e470c65d38d1e4c4e1e472f31.gif[/img]




[b]Tiny[/b] - Shrink your character down, and you can now hide behind any object (enemies will not see you). Normally you are hidden from view behind particularly tall objects, Tiny applies this to ALL objects.

[b]Strong[/b] - Add a small Damage Up, and move all objects super quick!

[b]HotSauce3[/b] - Add Fire to your equipped weapon. Stacks up to 2x, with greater ignite % for each level.

[b]Sharp[/b] - Small Damage Up to equipped weapon.
[h2]Unlockable Characters[/h2]

As seen above, there are now silhouettes of new Characters, which will be unlockable through different methods. Right now we just have the Egg, which is unlocked by getting lucky on the Passive Upgrade drop - this will appear as a Green upgrade token. Once unlocked, the Egg will be permanently selectable in the upgrade room. Simply run into the character and it will swap. Each character will have different stats and unique abilities. Egg has low HP and speed, but higher damage and knockback added to any weapon. Plus he's rad!

[h2]Monster-Doors[/h2]

I've been thinking of ways to slow the player down that didn't resort to just "wait until the timer completes", this wasn't very fun. So instead, doors have a chance to be yuckified with a Monster Door. These are immobile chunks of fleshy grossness that you'll need to destroy to pass. Initial version is the basic model, but there will be versions which can lash out, shoot projectiles, or alert the enemies of your location.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/d1e93af9bbf2b19df10832728d8c9b01e67f1a7d.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/3ef71744071f442077aed4a4c9833eb843e7512e.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Exit Goal[/h2]

Finding a fun exit / win-condition has been tricky, for now I've settled on the simplest : Every level has a number of Junk required to exit, which will be marked on the door. Collect enough Junk, you can safely leave. Easy peasy. Eventually this will lead way to a little boss fight, but for now, this is working out to be pretty fun and simple.

[h2]Bonus Level[/h2]

Find a Secret Coin to access the Bonus Level! This will reward an additional random Passive Upgrade. I think I've talked about this already but here it is some more. Planning to add different types of Bonus Stages in the future as well.



[h2]Check Your Keybinds![/h2]

Especially if you're playing on controller, check your in-game keybindings. I've been experimenting with different control schemes and I've landed on, for me, the best version yet. Feel free to play around with what suits you best, but this allows for true twin-stick action, and feels extremely fluid once you get the hang of it.

Movement - Left Stick
Aim - Right Stick
Attack - Right Trigger
Grab Object - Left Trigger
Rotate Object - Right Stick Press
Ability 1 - Left Bumper
Ability 2 - Right Bumper
Open Door / Use - Y / North Face-Button
Stationary (Lock Movement) - Hold A / South Face-Button



[h1]What's Next?[/h1]

Game is done! Congrats me!

Just kidding. We're only getting started!

Next update will bring in a different level setting, a new win-condition ("GET TO THE CHOPPA"), new enemies, upgrades, unlockable characters, and achievements. To be specific:

[list]
[*] [b]More Room Variants for Lab Levels,
[*] Mansion-Themed Level is Next,
[*] Overrun City to follow that,
[*] 3 New Enemy Types
[*] More Monster-Door Types
[*] Periodic Upgrades[/b]
[/list]

This is the general roadmap, really looking forward to you all playing this and letting me know what you think!

As always, greatly appreciate the support. If you'd like to leave direct feedback / talk about cool movies and stuff you're into / meme, we'd love to have you [url=https://discord.gg/r4GrmebTj7]join our SUPER SMALL but SUPER RAD Discord Server.[/url]

Love yall!
-Alex / Puke&Guts

notes.title: Major Update - Nov 16 2023
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello again folks. Run For Your Life took a big developmental break while I was busy with work and the real world. We're back now though![/h1]

[h2]I've spent the last few months cleaning things up and redoing the overall gameplay loop. There's a ton of changes, but I'll try to cover the biggest:[/h2]

[b]#1: The game now has a much more linear level structure[/b], 
which I'm hoping leads to better tension&release moments. A lot of the doors needed to progress through are time-activated, or require a key or button, etc. Forcing you into a chokepoint situation where you'll need to barricade and set traps until the path ahead is opened. 

[b]#2: Roguelite elements![/b] The abilities, weapons & passives are now rolled randomly at the start of each level, which should help out a lot with replayability and finding fun/janky combos. Cosmetics are still an unlock-system, which will persist through deaths.

[b]#3: Improved AI and Combat[/b]
This is always in progress, but I'm feeling pretty happy with the current combat system and enemy AI. There's a lot of small tweaks under the hood, so it may or may not be noticeable immediately.

I invite you to join the official Discord community to get early sneak peaks, be a part of the feedback and community-ideas process, and get yourself in the credits!

[h3]https://discord.gg/r4GrmebTj7[/h3]

Follow on Twitter as well to help boost visibility of the project! Word of mouth helps a ton <3
[h3]https://twitter.com/GutsPuke[/h3]

notes.title: An Update
notes.notes:
I've been working hard behind the scenes to improve enemy behavior, player control feel, and general code fixes to make the game run more smoothly. Thanks a million to anyone whos played, reviewed, given feedback, it means a lot (and helps me improve the game). I'm hopeful I'll be able to release more level updates and addons every few weeks, depending on how my real life job goes. Fingers crossed.

[u][b]Cool Changes:[/b][/u]

[b]Added Some New Levels[/b] - Dank Barns, Office, and the return of a smaller Lab level (now Lab 002). I'll be adding a few new settings in the next update, including a new Endless Mode level. Endless Mode in general needs some rehauling, it should be playable for now, but I'll be committing an update specifically to making it a better experience.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/7f7f47b3ccd38c3f9acacaa3331ba38006b1dd12.gif[/img]

[b]Attack & Range Visuals [/b]- This should help with combat, a lot of players were having trouble with missed attacks. Seeing the range of your selected weapon should help with this, as well there is a cooldown visual on the bottom left to help with timing attacks.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/d521804c7e18bb9f6b5795f10d1bbbde5e233988.gif[/img]

[b]Improved Mouse Response[/b] - Took a little tweaking but the mouse should feel much better to use. Big thanks to jlkennedy for the code assistance.

[b]Improved Enemy AI[/b] - This could be a few paragraphs long, so I'll summarize. Every enemy has an intelligence rating, and they'll seek out the player based on how intelligent they are (assuming you're not in their line of sight). As the level progresses they will narrow their field of focus, so you shouldn't have many boring end-game moments, but as always please let me know! I wanted to make sure the Enemy AI didn't just run directly at the player at all times, giving them the ability to try different paths makes for a more unpredictable (and fun?) game.

[b]Added Enemies[/b] - Two new enemies released this update are the Peeper and the Drone. Drones are headless zombies, on their own they will never be able to directly target the player (though they'll still chomp you if you get too close). 
Peepers are able to alert not just Drones but any enemy type of your exact location. All that improved AI stuff gets overridden, and the horde comes directly to you.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/9cddec72f932c971754dfd6d48f078eb34c87e53.gif[/img]

[b]Coop Fixed / Updated[/b] - Local and Steam Remote Coop should be working fine. In the shop menus, Player 2 can select their upgrades without needing Player 1 to navigate for them. During any level, just press Start on the Player 2 controller and you should be good to go. Let me know if you run into any problems.


Feel free to join the Puke&Guts Discord server to share feedback / ideas / memes, or follow on Twitter for updates. Hopefully I can keep the content coming. Thanks again for the support!

notes.title: Update Notes - April 6, 2021
notes.notes:
Some pretty hefty changes ahead. Quick form:

[b]-Improved AI, some basic object avoidance [/b]
This will continue to be refined, but you should see some enemies SOMETIMES bee-line towards you instead of just trashing everything around them. Still finding the balance on this. Ive already got some thoughts to improve the system further still.

[b]New Level-End System[/b]
When you collect every piece of junk, the timer will cut to one third of it's current time (down from one half), should make plays feel a little less arduous. 

Additionally, [b]there is now an exit-beacon that spawns[/b] randomly on the map. You can feed junk points into this to speed the timer up, and the points are stored in a bank upon level completion. The beacon can be destroyed, if this happens the exit-portal will spawn in a randomly selected area as before.

[b]Lowered Menu Music Volume[/b]
Sorry yall :P
Your SFX and Music volume settings should also stay persistent between runs, the intro music was the only part that wasn't playing nicely for a while.

[b]Hopefully fixed stuttering / hitching[/b]
Some bugs present themselves in such a way that your idiot-brain says "oh.. this is probably fine.. Im sure its nothing", only to persist and impact players. Never ignore these. A hugely helpful friend and tester noticed that sometimes the game gets into a bad habit of hitching every few seconds, something I've also run into occasionally. I think I've sorted this out, but please let me know if you run into this.

[b]"Invisible Wall" in Tutorial[/b]
Well lets be clear, the tutorial absolutely sucks at the moment, but Ive atleast fixed the reported "invisible wall" issue. It turns out the camera in this level wasn't rendering a newly created class ("Tall Props"), which is why it seemed like there was an invisible wall blocking the path.

notes.title: HUGE Mini-Update
notes.notes:
Making a game from scratch is easy. 
Finishing a game is absolutely ridiculous.

I have to apologize for the massive dropoff in updates and tweaks towards the end of last year. I returned to full-time work in the real world (or what passed for the real world..) and had a lot of trouble finding motivation to work on this. That said, I'm stoked for the features I've added since the last update, and there's a lot more in the works. 

Here's a rundown on what's new:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/b32fb3e5b3d6385382ff91d38ea073ede8ba2018.png[/img]
[b]Two New Levels[/b]
Let's start with the worst, and that's a pretty small bump in playable content. I've got templates, rough maps, and art assets for quite a few new levels, but I'm not happy with the gamefeel on those yet. Expect more levels on a more regular basis, now that I've got a lot of the boring work ironed out. So for now, I've included two smaller/shorter maps that feel reasonable quality to me: Spaceship01, and AlienPlanet01. I'll definitely be using these themes more often, but wanted to give a little taste atleast.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/77c822161d652642360e4911773a3bfbcfe4b4e9.png[/img]
[b]Fully Customizeable Player2[/b]
As I mentioned in a previous blog, I had to strip out co-op for a while to adjust to the new Input System with Unity. It was a pretty difficult change for my skill level, but I've finally wrangled it enough to work. So co-op is back, as well as the ability to now customize Player 2's cosmetics, abilities, weapon, and controls. Second player floats in the background of the Shop scene for now, like a little space-faring potato chip.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38449074/730518f234fa80ff42056b9ca1a2614e13b71852.png[/img]
[b]Aim-Control and Right-Stick Aiming[/b]
I've put a lot of work into the aiming mechanics, they were definitely on the primitive side previously. You now have the ability to hold down an Aim key, which will show a crosshair on screen. Control the position of the crosshair with your regular movement inputs, for much better precision. Controller-players can also use their Right-Stick to aim freely while running. 


[b]Re-map Controls In-Game[/b]
Following on the previous point, you're now able to fully rebind your controls in-game, and they auto-save, so this should be persistent between play sessions. I'm working on getting the mouse to function properly, so KBM players have a much better time of it, but I wasn't able to get that working in time for today's update. 
[b]Improved Hit Detection[/b]
I had some issues with frame-timing when the player attacked, resulting in some missed hits. Unacceptable. I've made some changes to the way the hit-detection works, and it should be perfect now.
[b]Improved AI[/b]
Enemies now have the ability to *attempt* to dodge your energy blasts, depending on their intelligence, some are more successful than others. 
[b]New Enemies[/b]
There are a few new enemies in this update (and more still yet to be used), one is a variant of the runner-zombie which explodes on contact, and the other is your standard Alien dude. Expect better Aliens in the future.
[b]More Distinct Weapon Differences[/b]
This one is still in progress, but definitely on display if you manage to unlock The Game-Dev. I always thought it would be funny to have a weapon that "reprograms" elements of the game. The Game-Dev now modifies the properties of the enemy attacked, including it's size, colour, stats, and whether it's friendly or hostile. Expect more changes in the future, both to The Game-Dev and the other weapons.


It's been a while, so I honestly don't remember if there are more changes I've added and forgotten to list. As always, your feedback is hugely appreciated, and thanks a million to anyone who's given this game a shot. I'm going to keep working on this game, with the ultimate goal being to have functioning Multiplayer modes. This update should be live within the hour.

Feel free to join the discord server for direct feedback / suggestions / criticism:
https://discord.gg/hDvETYs

Follow on Twitter for teasers and polls:
https://twitter.com/GutsPuke

Thanks and have an awesome day!

notes.title: Community-Feedback Update 0.1
notes.notes:
First of all : You guys are amazing. Thank you for trying out this weirdo nonsense game and for your amazing feedback, suggestions, and compliments. Being a solo dev is a ton of work, so hearing nice words, seeing cool reviews, it means a ton.

This is a smaller update aimed at some of the more pressing issues and annoyances - there's still lots to be done, but this should make things a little smoother. I started the day unsure of how much I'd be able to finish, but I think it's a pretty solid little update for now.

Stay tuned for a much bigger Community-Feedback Update - you can see some of the features coming down the pipe in the Shop! More details on that to come.

[b]For now here's the mostly complete list of fixes and changes:[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]Level costs are higher, but so too are the rewards for completing a level.[/b]
[*] [b]Cosmetic costs are now lower, each wearable piece of gear is now 50JP flat.[/b]
[*] [b]The level select screen is now a little easier to understand[/b] what is currently selected, with an error sound indicating if an option is not available or the requirements haven't been met yet.
[*] [b]Autosave![/b] Whether your survive or die, the game will save your progress, unlocks and points. Just make sure to use the Continue button next time you load the game :P
[*] [b]Gameover screen now waits a little before allowing you to move on[/b] - I didn't realize how button mash-y the game might be, and a lot of players were dying and immediately being skipped through the game-over screen. Fixed!
[*] [b]The shop now provides a preview of the cosmetics[/b] as well as the price (or if it's already owned), hopefully easing some confusion and accidental unlocks!
[*] [b]Endless Mode waves now end early if the player manages to kill every enemy in a wave.[/b] Once again, not something I anticipated happening, but some of you folks are absolute beasts. This should allow for more aggressive players to get real deep into the waves at a much quicker pace. Good luck!
[*] [b]Endless Mode respawns Junk Points on every setup phase[/b], but they frequently bounced in and out of existence, kind of funny, super annoying. I believe I've sorted this now. Let me know if you get cheated out of any tasty junk still.
[*] [b]Health and Energy now have some backing to help visualize[/b] just how low you are on these resources. Small tweak, bigggg difference.
[*] [b]Controls can be viewed in the Options Menu[/b] - I'm waiting until I get some money together to purchase Rewired, which from what I've found, is the only sane way to get rebinding controls to work with Unity. I don't get it, but it seems thats the only sensible option. For now you can still re-bind at load. Sorry!
[*] [b]Doors now respond much better to Energy and Explosive blasts.[/b] You've been warned.
[*] [b]Energy Balls now have a maximum size.[/b] No more nukes :P
[*] [b]Player Cosmetics will now flash when the player takes damage[/b], small thing I'd overlooked. Much easier to visualize when you're getting chewed on now.
[/list]

[b]Players were sometimes experiencing pretty bad hit-detection.[/b] I believe I've narrowed down the issues, and while this won't be a 100% fix, it should help in about 95% of instances. A more robust attack-detection system is already in the works, but there's only so much I can manage in a day :P Here's the notes on that:
[list]
[*] [b]Re-enabled V-Sync[/b] : I initially had some suspicion about frame-timing being the culprit with players attacks not always registering, but I think I've found the real issue, so this is back on. Smooth!
[*] [b]Player direction will temporarily lock when attacking.[/b] I noticed some issues with hits not being detected, and I've narrowed it down to the fact that depending on which way you're facing or moving, your attack range changes. Rapidly switching directions can have some undesired effects, so I've locked it in place - my early testing makes this feel a lot better, but as always, would love your feedback.
[/list]

Okay that's a ton of word-nonsense, so I'll leave it there for now. I'm looking forward to hearing any additional feedback, and I'm stoked for the next Community Update - lots of cool ideas coming your way, and largely by you!

Follow for frequent updates on Twitter, and consider joining the Discord! It's ultra quiet right now, but it's a great way to get feedback to me super quickly, as well as some early announcements. Cheers!

Twitter: @GutsPuke
Discord: https://discord.gg/TGaj29
Facebook: facebook.com/RFYLgame

notes.title: A small (big) update.
notes.notes:
Recently added a counter to the top left to show how many [b]Pieces of Junk[/b] remain in a level, this has been requested by a few players and it absolutely makes sense.

I've also added the ability to [b]rotate[/b] most props in the game, along with corresponding broken-prop versions to match. There's still a small number of props left to do this for, and some will simply not have rotate functionality (barrels, crates, etc).
